column117: Generation of the parent T cell clone A6 was previously described in the reference: Utz et al. (1996) J Virol. 70(2): 843-851 [PMID: 8551623]. The T cell clone was established from a HTLV-1-seropositive patient diagnosed with HAM/TSP 13 years prior to the study. CD8+ T cells were sorted from PBMC and stimulated in vitro with the epitope and cloned by limiting dilution. The S3-4 single-chain TCR variant (scTv) of the A6 TCR was generated in a directed evolution experiment designed to shift the peptide speciﬁcity of the well-characterized A6 TCR from the viral Tax antigen to the MART-1 tumor antigen. The library from which S3-4 evolved incorporated mutations in three CDR loops, utilizing both degenerate and “either/or” mutations in CDR1α, CDR3α, and CDR3β. S3-4 possesses six mutations distributed across these three loops.

column117: A 27-year-old patient developed recurrent AML with both extramedullary chloromas and minimal residual disease (MRD) in the bone marrow 7 months after receiving a second matched, unrelated donor HCT for relapsed refractory disease. The patient was treated with local radiation and systemic salvage chemotherapy, which achieved remission as evidenced by no evaluable disease, and then received an infusion of donor-derived T (TCR-C4), specific for the epitope. The patient remained in remission without further therapy for 368 days before exhibiting recurrent AML with both a bladder chloroma and flow-cytometric evidence of MRD in the bone marrow. He then received reinduction chemotherapy followed by a second T (TCR-C4) infusion on day 471 after the 1st infusion with T cells derived from the same pool of transduced cells originally infused. A second patient who received T(TCR-C4) and had blasts available before and after T cell infusion was also analyzed.
column129: CD8+ T cells in PBMCs and bone marrow were collected before and at defined timepoints after T (TCR-C4 ) infusions and stained with the epitope/HLA-A*02:01 multimers. Comparable high T (TCR-C4) frequencies were observed in the bone marrow at days 28 and 368.
